properties.description: Moon (2009), directed by Duncan Jones and starring Sam Rockwell, Kevin Spacey and Dominique McElligott, is a low-budget, near-future science fiction drama that blends psychological mystery with emotional character work. The film emphasizes intimate performances, practical production design, and a meditative tone to explore loneliness, family longing and ethical questions about cloning and exploitation.
properties.plot_summary: An astronaut nearing the end of a three-year solo contract on a lunar mining base begins experiencing hallucinations and memory disorientation while working with the station's robotic assistant. The discovery triggers a tense, intimate struggle to piece together stolen memories, confront corporate exploitation, and find a way home.

properties.description: Primer (2004) is a low-budget independent science-fiction drama-thriller written and directed by Shane Carruth and starring Shane Carruth, David Sullivan, and Casey Gooden. The film follows a small group of entrepreneurial engineers who accidentally invent a crude time-travel device and gradually descend into secrecy, duplications, and escalating paranoia as they exploit and fight over its use. The narrative emphasizes ethical dilemmas, trust breakdowns, and the unforeseen consequences of iterative experimentation, delivered in a terse, clinical visual style that rewards attentive, repeat viewing. Emotionally, the movie is intellectually unsettling and claustrophobic, prioritizing moral ambiguity and procedural realism over conventional exposition.
properties.plot_summary: A group of entrepreneurial engineers working out of a garage accidentally build a small, crude time machine capable of sending users back short intervals. At first they run controlled experiments and exploit the device for minor gains, but iterative use creates overlapping timelines and competing agendas. Secrecy, duplications, and escalating paranoia strain friendships as the characters face ethical dilemmas and attempt to control the unpredictable consequences of manipulating causality.

properties.description: Gattaca (1997), written and directed by Andrew Niccol, is a science-fiction drama starring Ethan Hawke, Uma Thurman, and Jude Law. As he advances toward a scheduled mission, a murder a week before launch triggers a forensic investigation that threatens to expose him as a suspect. The story examines the personal and social costs of a system that ranks people by DNA.

properties.description: The Lobster (2015), directed by Yorgos Lanthimos and co-written with Efthimis Filippou, is a dystopian drama/romantic science fiction thriller starring Colin Farrell, Rachel Weisz and Jessica Barden. Set at a government-run hotel where singles have forty-five days to find a partner or be transformed into animals and exiled, the film uses absurdist satire and deadpan performances to interrogate conformity and the politics of intimacy. Its tone is bleak yet darkly comic, pairing formal, restrained visual design with provocative examinations of identity, love, and authoritarian social control.
properties.plot_summary: In a dystopian near future, single people are sent to a government-run hotel where they must find a romantic partner within forty-five days or be surgically transformed into an animal and expelled into the surrounding woods. The system enforces arbitrary compatibility rules and punishes nonconformity, while a fugitive contingent of ‘loners’ survive outside the city under strict, oppositional rules. The story follows a newly arrived man as he navigates the hotel’s ritualized dating, the moral compromises it requires, and the bleakly absurd consequences of choosing love or freedom.
